title: Tonal Analysis Through Listening and Notation
learners: Students can read treble and bass clefs and identify major/minor triads.
coursePurpose: Connect heard tonal function, notated evidence, and analytical claims across short progressions.
outcomes: Label a cadence from notated and aural evidence.
Explain a non-chord tone in relation to voice leading.
Revise an analysis after comparing an alternate hearing.

sourcePacket.content: In C major: D4-F4-A4 resolves to G3-B3-D4, then C4-E4-G4. The packet identifies ii6-V-I and does not establish a deceptive cadence.
A longer chord is not necessarily structurally stronger; duration alone does not establish harmonic function.

localConstraints: Notation and answer keys must agree.
Provide a non-audio alternative that preserves the analytical construct.
Do not claim one hearing is the only possible reading without evidence.
adversarialConditions: Duration is offered as a false proxy for function.
